newsitem.title: CYPRUS: SOCCER-COMMISSION TO INVESTIGATE CYPRUS FIXING CLAIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COMMISSION TO INVESTIGATE CYPRUS FIXING CLAIM.

text.p: An official Cypriot commission is to investigate allegations of match fixing in a World Cup qualifier between Cyprus and Bulgaria on December 14, a Cyprus Football Association official said on Friday.
The commission is to be appointed by the Cyprus Sports Association (KOA), which is due to meet on Tuesday to decide on its responsibilities, an F.A. official said.
"The F.A. has decided to assign the investigation to KOA because it wants a completely independent inquiry," the official said.

The allegations, reported extensively by the local media, suggest players on the island's national team placed considerable bets for Cyprus to lose to Bulgaria in the match, played in the southern coastal town of Limassol.
The reports do not mention any specific player, but football authorities admit the sums bet on the match - up to 10 times the normal - were enough to arouse suspicion.
F.A. officials have publicly stated that up to 30,000 pounds ($64,000) was placed on the game. The usual sum bet was around 3,000 pounds.
Bookmakers even rejected bets because the sums placed made them suspicious. The F.A. has asked for a government inquiry into bookmakers' accounts to ascertain who and how much money was actually bet.

The F.A. wants a ban on all betting involving national teams and local teams. Legislation pending approval in parliament empowers the Finance Ministry, which charges 25 per cent for every bet placed, to ban such bets and revoke the licences of establishments accepting them illegally.
